sources_admitted.evidence: Every record the page cites is pinned under data/sources/iowa-army-detonation and data/sources/coverage with its text and hash; the X posts were admitted from saved post text and the Army's map page from a rendered image with its OCR, because capture drops map labels.

derived_numbers_computed.evidence: The page computes nothing; every number in the data module (68 drums, 9,700 pounds, the 100 and 60 mile air reach, the 40 and 25 mile dust areas, the 0.18 edge, the permit's 5-day, 48-hour, 6-hour and 24-hour deadlines) is printed on an admitted record named beside it.

outlet_claims_verified.evidence: The Intercept's 'blanketing communities ... up to 100 miles away' is checked against the Army's map legend, EPA's all-lead modeling rule and the groups' own reading of the dust maps; CBS News Chicago's northwest Illinois line against Illinois EPA's release and Linn County's note that Friday's maps do not apply to Monday.

live_elements_guarded.evidence: The page has no live element; the maps, statements, posts and coverage are saved copies dated in the records list, and the page says Monday's maps are not yet published.

subject_page_updated.evidence: A new iowa-army-detonation subject page and data module list the 68 drums and the permit's five-day minimum for the first plume map, with a listing description covering the delay to Monday and the court petition.
